changelog/CHANGELOG.html.title: Changelog | FMOD Plus
changelog/CHANGELOG.html.summary: Changelog This document records the major changes to FMOD Plus. [1.7.2] - 2026-08-11 Changed Moved the About window to the Bootstrap Editor assembly so it can be used regardless of whether FMOD is installed. Changed the About window's UXML, USS, logo, and package.json resolution to use GUIDs and AssetDatabase.GUIDToAssetPath instead of fixed paths or serialized references. Refined the About UI structure and styles, and added a diagnosable fallback message when loading the package version fails. Fixed Fixed the About window content not rendering when a serialized UXML or package.json reference was not assigned. [1.7.1] - 2026-08-11 Changed Organized the fields, properties, public methods, and private helpers in KeyReference by responsibility. Expanded the XML documentation for KeyReference.Key, Guid, Path, ToString(), and the Key lookup APIs. Organized the fields, overrides, private helpers, and internal enum in FMODEventTrigger by responsibility. [1.7.0] - 2026-08-11 Added Added APIs to KeyReference for safely retrieving Events and initial parameters from Global and Local Key Lists. Added EditMode tests for default Key creation, duplicate prevention, immediate lookup after modification, and null-data handling in AudioPathByString. Added EditMode tests that verify the Unity-version-appropriate static field initialization policy. Changed Separated playback, command, and event-handling responsibilities in FMODAudioSource, CommandSender, and FMODEventTrigger, and revised their public API documentation. Changed LocalKeyList to encapsulate serialized fields and provide value-oriented lookup APIs (Count, TryGetEvent, TryGetParameters, and TryGetEventAndParameters). Changed Command Sender and Editor UI code that references Local Key Lists to use LocalKeyList lookup APIs instead of directly iterating serialized arrays. Removed duplicated FMOD EventReference.Find code from KeyReference and clarified the responsibilities and null handling of the Key List reference model. Split AudioType, EventRefCallback, KeyAndPath, EventReferenceByKey, and AudioPathByString from FMODPlusUtility.cs into files organized by responsibility. Changed FMODPlusUtility.Length to safely handle empty Events, invalid Event Descriptions, and lookup failures. Expanded the public API XML documentation for AudioPathByString, EventRefAtKey, and KeyAndPath. Applied [AutoStaticsCleanup] to mutable static fields on Unity 6.5 or newer, while retaining Enter Play Mode initialization callbacks on Unity 6.4 or older. Replaced the legacy UXML factory/traits implementation in SimpleBaseField with the Unity 6 [UxmlElement] and [UxmlAttribute] APIs. Expanded the public API XML documentation for Key List ScriptableObjects and Local Key List, and improved null safety. Fixed Fixed exceptions or unnecessary error logs that could occur with null Local Key List collections, entries, parameter arrays, or empty Key lookups. Fixed AudioPathByString returning stale Events or parameters from its internal Dictionary cache after its public list was modified. Fixed default Keys being unavailable when an intermediate number was unused, and Keys with matching substrings being treated as duplicates. Fixed EventRefCallback.TryGetClip throwing an exception for an invalid ClipStyle. Fixed Global Key List singletons and Editor UI caches retaining previous state when re-entering Play Mode with Domain Reload disabled. Fixed alignment callbacks being registered more than once when a custom UI field was reattached to a panel. Removed Removed the legacy Event, AllowNonRigidbodyDoppler, UpdateActiveAudioSource(), and writable EventInstance APIs from FMODAudioSource. Removed the legacy public ClipList field, top-level EventRefList, conversion ContextMenu, and old TryFind*/TryGetValue APIs from LocalKeyList. [1.7.0-beta.1] - 2026-08-11 Added Added the UI Toolkit-based FMOD/FMOD Plus/Setup window. Added automatic Korean/English localization of the Setup window based on the system language. Added detection of FMOD Integration under Assets and migration to Embedded UPM. Added UPM SemVer conversion for FMOD Integration versions and automatic recovery of the FMOD.meta GUID. Added migration preflight checks, file-move rollback, and Settings/Cache preservation. Added a Global Key List Editor Window that combines AMB, BGM, and SFX. Added Key-name search to Global and Local Key Lists. Added a detail panel for editing the selected Event and initial parameters. Added automatic application of the FMOD Studio Listener icon. Changed Changed FMOD Plus to the com.nkstudio.fmodplus Embedded UPM package structure. Changed FMOD package detection to use an asmdef Version Define for com.firelight.fmod-for-unity versions in [2.2.0,3.0.0). Changed Runtime and Editor assemblies to compile only when FMOD is installed. Rebuilt the Global and Local Key List editing UI with UXML/USS-based UI Toolkit. Changed LocalKeyList to directly inherit MonoBehaviour, and the AMB/BGM/SFX lists to directly inherit ScriptableObject. Changed FMODAudioSource to update distance-based playback state directly without an FMOD source hook. Added minimum/maximum sizes and narrow-width responsive layout to the Setup window. Fixed Fixed the selected Key List index becoming incorrect after searching or Undo/Redo. Fixed fields and buttons being pushed sideways when the Local Key List Inspector was narrow. Fixed initial parameter lists sometimes failing to refresh after changing an Event. Fixed the FMOD migration button remaining disabled because AssetDatabase remembered a deleted package path. Prevented path errors caused by including FMOD Settings and Cache in Packages. Improved rollback ordering so an original meta file or package.json is not left behind when a file write fails during migration. Removed Removed separate Global Key List menus for AMB, BGM, and SFX. Removed the decorative dedicated Inspector UI from Global Key List ScriptableObjects. Removed automatic registration of the legacy USE_FMOD and FMODPlus Scripting Defines. Removed hooks that directly modified FMOD RuntimeManager and StudioListener Editor sources. [1.6.4]-Beta - 2023-11-13 Added Added PlayThisOneShot to FMOD Audio Source. [1.6.3]-Beta - 2023-10-24 Fixed Fixed Show Info being hidden because the KeyList label text was offset. [1.6.2]-Beta - 2023-10-24 Added Added KeyList. Fixed Added KeyListSO and KeyListMono for developers using Inspector assets such as Odin. [1.6.1]-Beta - 2023-10-24 Added Added a UI Toolkit Inspector converter for FMOD Plus. Fixed Suppressed warnings for items that do not use an audio style. [1.6.0]-Beta - 2023-10-24 Added Added Key List support to Audio Source. Fixed Redefined the Command Sender concept. [1.5.0]-Beta - 2023-10-17 Added Added EventRefAtKey so an FMOD Key List can be drawn on a MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject. Fixed Changed all Key Lists to use the EventRefAtKey approach. Fixed Key Lists showing only the header and not opening. [1.4.2]-Beta - 2023-10-16 Fixed Changed FMOD Audio Source playOnAwake to run in Enable instead of Start. Changed FMOD Audio Source to call Stop when disabled. [1.4.1]-Beta - 2023-10-16 Fixed Removed NKEditorUtility. [1.4.0]-Beta - 2023-10-16 Fixed Converted all Key Lists to UI Toolkit. manual/command-sender.html.title: Command Sender | FMOD Plus
manual/command-sender.html.summary: Command Sender CommandSender forwards an Inspector-configured command to an FMODAudioSource or the FMOD Studio System. A UnityEvent or FMODEventTrigger can always call the same SendCommand() method while the Sender selects playback, stopping, key-off, Local Parameter, or Global Parameter behavior. Create a Command Sender Add a CommandSender in either of the following ways: Select GameObject > Audio > FMOD > Command Sender. On an existing GameObject, select FMOD Studio > FMOD Plus > FMOD Command Sender from Add Component. Every behavior except Global Parameter requires a target FMODAudioSource. The basic setup is to assign it directly to Audio Source. Behaviour types Behaviour Target Action Play FMOD Audio Source Selects an Event, applies Parameters, and starts playback. Stop FMOD Audio Source Stops the current Event with the selected Fade option. Key Off FMOD Audio Source Releases a sustain point on the current Event. Parameter FMOD Audio Source Applies Local Parameters to the current Event. Global Parameter FMOD Studio System Changes a project-wide Parameter value. CommandSender has no Pause or Mute behavior. Use FMODAudioSource.Pause() and mute directly for those operations. Send On Awake Despite its name, Send On Awake invokes SendCommand() from OnEnable, not Awake. The command is sent when the GameObject first becomes enabled. Disabling and enabling it again sends the command again. When a target or Key is assigned at runtime, disable this option or configure execution order so the command cannot run before the assignment is complete. Call SendCommand directly Code can execute the configured Behaviour and Inspector values through the single SendCommand() method. using FMODPlus; using UnityEngine; public class CommandButton : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] private CommandSender commandSender; public void Execute() { commandSender.SendCommand(); } } Connect CommandSender.SendCommand to a Unity UI Button or UI Toolkit UnityEvent. The caller remains the same even when the configured command becomes more complex. Connect an Event Trigger Set the FMODEventTrigger Trigger Type to Command Sender, then assign the Sender to Command Sender. The Trigger invokes SendCommand() when its configured Send Event occurs. The Command Sender target does not use the Event Trigger Stop Event. To stop from a Trigger, create a separate Command Sender with Stop behavior and invoke it from the desired Event. See Event Trigger for the available Event conditions.

manual/event-trigger.html.title: Event Trigger | FMOD Plus
manual/event-trigger.html.summary: Event Trigger FMODEventTrigger builds on the FMOD for Unity EventHandler to forward Unity GameObject, physics, mouse, and UI pointer events to an FMODAudioSource or CommandSender. It can play a Snapshot when an object enters an area or send a Parameter command from UI input without custom code. Add the component On the GameObject that should detect the Event, select FMOD Studio > FMOD Plus > FMOD Event Trigger from Add Component. When using Trigger or Collision events, also configure the required Collider and Rigidbody on this GameObject. The actual Audio Source or Command Sender can be on the same or a different GameObject. Trigger Type Audio Source Set Trigger Type to Audio Source to display these fields: Field Action Audio Source The FMODAudioSource that receives playback and stop commands Play Event Invokes Play() for the selected Unity Event Stop Event Invokes Stop() for the selected Unity Event Stop() uses the target Audio Source Allow Fadeout When Stopping setting. Command Sender Set Trigger Type to Command Sender to display these fields: Field Action Command Sender The CommandSender to execute Send Event Invokes SendCommand() for the selected Unity Event Stop Event is hidden for a Command Sender target and ignored at runtime. Tip To stop through a Command Sender, create a Sender with Stop behavior and execute it from Send Event. Supported Events Select None when that action should never execute. Category Event When it occurs Lifecycle ObjectStart When Start runs Lifecycle ObjectDestroy When the GameObject is destroyed Lifecycle ObjectEnable When the component becomes enabled Lifecycle ObjectDisable When the component becomes disabled 3D Trigger TriggerEnter, TriggerExit When another 3D Collider enters or exits the Trigger 2D Trigger TriggerEnter2D, TriggerExit2D When another 2D Collider enters or exits the Trigger 3D Collision CollisionEnter, CollisionExit When a 3D Collision begins or ends 2D Collision CollisionEnter2D, CollisionExit2D When a 2D Collision begins or ends Object Mouse ObjectMouseEnter, ObjectMouseExit When the pointer enters or exits a Collider area Object Mouse ObjectMouseDown, ObjectMouseUp When a Collider is pressed or released UI Pointer UIMouseEnter, UIMouseExit When the pointer enters or exits a UI area UI Pointer UIMouseDown, UIMouseUp When a UI element is pressed or released

manual/fmod-audio-source.html.title: FMOD Audio Source | FMOD Plus
manual/fmod-audio-source.html.summary: FMOD Audio Source FMODAudioSource is a component that plays FMOD Events from a GameObject, much like Unity's AudioSource. You can use the same component for sounds that need continuous control, such as background music, as well as parameterized effects and 3D audio. This page walks through the complete workflow, from selecting and playing an Event to controlling it at runtime. Add the component Add FMODAudioSource in either of these ways: Select GameObject > Audio > FMOD > Audio Source to create a new Audio Source GameObject. On an existing GameObject, select FMOD Studio > FMOD Plus > FMOD Audio Source from Add Component. The Scene needs an FMOD Studio Listener for you to hear the sound. The Listener is usually added to the Main Camera. Select an Event Use Clip Style in the Inspector to choose how the Event is assigned. Select an Event directly Use the following setup when a GameObject always plays one specific Event: Set Clip Style to Event Reference. Select an FMOD Event in the Event field. Select from a Key List Set Clip Style to Key when multiple Audio Sources should share Events by name, or when you want to manage an Event and its initial Parameters together. For a Global Key, enable Use Global Key List and select AMB, BGM, or SFX. For a Scene or Prefab Key List, disable Use Global Key List and assign a LocalKeyList to Key List. Select the entry to play from Key. Changing Clip Style clears the previous selection, so select the Event or Key again. See Global and Local Key Lists to learn how to create Keys. Play a sound Play automatically when enabled To play as soon as the GameObject becomes enabled: Select an Event or Key. Enable Play On Awake. Enter Play Mode. Enabling the GameObject or component again requests playback again. When it is disabled, the sound stops according to Allow Fadeout When Stopping. Play from code or a UnityEvent To play at a specific time, such as from a button, Timeline, or game state, disable Play On Awake and call Play(). using FMODPlus; using UnityEngine; public class MusicController : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource; public void PlayMusic() { audioSource.Play(); } } In a UnityEvent, select FMODAudioSource.Play() on the target GameObject to connect the same action without another script. Calling Play() does nothing when no Event is assigned. Control playback Choose how to stop Set Allow Fadeout When Stopping under Advanced Controls, then call Stop() to use that setting. public void StopMusic() { audioSource.Stop(); } Use Stop(bool) when you need to choose the stop behavior for each call. // Use the fadeout authored in FMOD Studio. audioSource.Stop(true); // Stop the sound immediately. audioSource.Stop(false); The actual fade curve and duration for Stop(true) must be authored on the Event in FMOD Studio. Without a fadeout or AHDSR release, it may sound similar to an immediate stop. Pause and resume Call Pause() to stop at the current playback position and UnPause() to continue from that position. public void PauseMusic() { audioSource.Pause(); } public void ResumeMusic() { audioSource.UnPause(); } Mute playback Enable Mute in the Inspector or set mute to true to pause the current sound. Disable Mute or set it to false to continue playback. audioSource.mute = true; audioSource.mute = false; Adjust Volume and Pitch Adjust the current sound's volume and playback rate in the Inspector or from code. audioSource.Volume = 0.5f; audioSource.Pitch = 1.2f; Volume is limited to the range from 0 to 1. Pitch is limited to the range from -3 to 3. Values set before playback are used the next time the Event plays. Change the Event at runtime To switch music or effects as the game progresses, assign a new EventReference to clip, then call Play(). using FMODPlus; using FMODUnity; using UnityEngine; public class StageMusic : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource; [SerializeField] private EventReference stageTwoMusic; public void ChangeToStageTwo() { audioSource.clip = stageTwoMusic; audioSource.Play(); } } Changing clip immediately clears the sound that was previously playing. The new Event does not start automatically, so call Play() when it should begin. Use Event Parameters Parameters let you change states such as a music stage, effect intensity, or surface type without replacing the Event. Apply initial values when playback starts After selecting an Event, Initial Parameter Values appears in the Inspector. Expand Initial Parameter Values. Select a Local Parameter from Add. Set the value to use when playback starts. The registered values are applied every time Play() starts the sound. When using a Key List, you can configure Parameters from the Event linked to the selected Key. Change a Parameter during playback Pass the Parameter name and value to SetParameter(). public void ChangeStage(float value) { audioSource.SetParameter("Stage", value); } Pass true as the third argument to ignore the Seek Speed authored in FMOD Studio and apply the value immediately. audioSource.SetParameter("Stage", 1f, true); Apply multiple Parameters together Create an array of ParamRef values and pass it to ApplyParameter(). audioSource.ApplyParameter(new[] { new ParamRef { Name = "Stage", Value = 1f }, new ParamRef { Name = "Intensity", Value = 0.75f }, }); If a matching name is registered under Initial Parameter Values, the new value is also used for subsequent playback. Use a Parameter ID When changing a Parameter frequently, such as every frame, look up and store its FMOD PARAMETER_ID once instead of using its name each time. using FMOD.Studio; using FMODUnity; private PARAMETER_ID stageParameterId; private bool hasStageParameter; private void CacheStageParameter() { EventDescription eventDescription = RuntimeManager.GetEventDescription(audioSource.clip); hasStageParameter = eventDescription.getParameterDescriptionByName( "Stage", out PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION description) == FMOD.RESULT.OK; if (hasStageParameter) stageParameterId = description.id; } public void ChangeStageFrequently(float value) { if (hasStageParameter) audioSource.SetParameter(stageParameterId, value); } Call CacheStageParameter() once after selecting or changing the Event, then use the stored ID through ChangeStageFrequently(). Play short effects as one-shots One-shots are best for short sounds that can overlap, such as button clicks, impacts, and footsteps. Required behavior Method to use Repeat or overlap a short sound PlayOneShot() Stop, pause, or key off the sound later Set clip and use Play() Play the currently selected Event once at the current position PlayThisOneShot() Play an Event Reference or path using FMODPlus; using FMODUnity; using UnityEngine; public class EffectPlayer : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource; [SerializeField] private EventReference hitEffect; public void PlayHit() { audioSource.PlayOneShot(hitEffect, 1f, transform.position); } public void PlayHitByPath() { audioSource.PlayOneShot("event:/SFX/Hit", 1f, transform.position); } } When omitted, volumeScale defaults to 1 and position defaults to Vector3.zero. Pass transform.position or an impact point explicitly so a 3D effect plays at the intended location. You cannot later control a one-shot with this component's Stop(), Pause(), or KeyOff(). Use regular Play() when the sound needs control after it starts. Play with Parameters Pass a name and value directly for a single Parameter. audioSource.PlayOneShot( hitEffect, "Surface", 2f, volumeScale: 1f, position: transform.position); Pass a collection of ParamRef values for multiple Parameters. var parameters = new[] { new ParamRef { Name = "Surface", Value = 2f }, new ParamRef { Name = "Intensity", Value = 0.5f }, }; audioSource.PlayOneShot(hitEffect, parameters, 1f, transform.position); Play the currently selected Event PlayThisOneShot() plays the current clip once at this GameObject's position and current Volume. audioSource.PlayThisOneShot(); It does not automatically pass Initial Parameter Values. Use a PlayOneShot() overload that accepts Parameters when they are required. Continue past a sustain point When an FMOD Studio Event is authored to wait at a sustain point, call KeyOff() to continue to its next section. public void ContinueDialogue() { audioSource.KeyOff(); } TriggerCue() sends the same command to the current Event. audioSource.TriggerCue(); There is no audible change when the Event has no sustain point. Play 3D audio When you select an Event authored as 3D in FMOD Studio, its sound follows the GameObject containing FMODAudioSource. Configure the Event as 3D in FMOD Studio and rebuild the Bank. Select the Event on FMODAudioSource in Unity. Confirm that the Main Camera or player has an FMOD Studio Listener. Place or move the Audio Source GameObject at the desired position. Velocity is supplied according to how the GameObject moves: When a Rigidbody or Rigidbody2D is present, its Velocity is used. When moving the Transform directly without a Rigidbody, enable Non-Rigidbody Velocity if the sound needs Doppler. Do not enable Non-Rigidbody Velocity when a Rigidbody is present. Change attenuation distances Enable Override Attenuation when only this Audio Source should use different attenuation distances from the FMOD Studio Event. Min: the distance where attenuation begins Max: the maximum attenuation distance Max cannot be less than Min. You can also adjust both distances with the radius handles in the Scene view. This setting is available only for 3D Events. Handle continuous Events outside the maximum distance When Stop Events Outside Max Distance is enabled in FMOD for Unity settings, a continuous 3D Event stops while the Listener is outside Max Distance and starts again from the beginning when it returns inside. Parameters changed during playback are applied again. A 3D one-shot uses the position supplied when it starts. Use regular Play() instead when the sound must keep following a moving object or needs to be stopped later. Control a Snapshot Select an FMOD Snapshot from the Event field, then use Play() and Stop() to enable and disable it like a regular Event. public void EnterCave() { audioSource.Play(); } public void ExitCave() { audioSource.Stop(); } Use Event Trigger when a trigger volume or Unity Event should control the Snapshot. Options to use when needed Prepare the first playback For an Event that must start immediately after it is requested, enable Advanced Controls > Preload Sample Data. Preparing the selected Event's sample data ahead of time can reduce the first-play delay, but it may increase memory usage. Use it selectively for frequently used sounds that need an immediate response instead of enabling it for every Event. Allow playback only once Enable Trigger Once to ignore additional Play() requests after the current Event plays for the first time. Re-enabling the GameObject or calling Play() after Stop() does not play the same Event again. Assigning a different Event to clip at runtime allows that new Event to play once. Use this option for notifications or sequences that must occur only once. Check playback state and time Read the state properties to display playback progress in UI or prevent duplicate playback. if (!audioSource.isPlaying) { audioSource.Play(); } float duration = audioSource.Length; float currentTime = audioSource.Time; float progress = duration > 0f ? currentTime / duration : 0f; What to check Property Whether the current sound is playing or sustaining isPlaying Whether playback requested by Play() is still active IsActive Total duration of the selected Event in seconds Length Current playback position in seconds Time IsActive can remain true while a 3D Event is outside its maximum distance and currently inaudible. Use isPlaying when you need the actual playback state. Use EventInstance only when you need to call low-level FMOD functionality directly. Always check audioSource.EventInstance.isValid() first. Sounds played as one-shots cannot be controlled through this property.

manual/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | FMOD Plus
manual/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started 1. Verify the installation Open FMOD > FMOD Plus > Setup and confirm that a supported FMOD for Unity package is active. Resolve the first Console compilation error before adding FMOD Plus components. 2. Verify the listener Ensure that the camera has an FMOD Studio Listener component attached instead of Unity's default Audio Listener. You can easily replace it by right-clicking the Unity Audio Listener component and selecting Change FMOD Studio Listener. 3. Create an audio source Create a GameObject from GameObject > Audio > FMOD > Audio Source. This creates a GameObject with an FMODAudioSource component. Select the created GameObject and find the FMODAudioSource component in the Inspector. Set Clip Style to Event Reference. In Event, select the FMOD Event you want to play. Enable Play On Awake. Enter Play Mode. The selected Event plays automatically when the GameObject is enabled. If you cannot hear the Event, confirm that the FMOD banks are available and that the camera has the FMOD Studio Listener configured in step 2.

manual/index.html.title: FMOD Plus | FMOD Plus
manual/index.html.summary: FMOD Plus FMOD Plus provides runtime components and Editor tools that make FMOD for Unity feel closer to Unity's built-in AudioSource workflow. Use FMODAudioSource, Global and Local Key Lists, Command Sender, and Event Trigger to configure common audio behavior without coupling gameplay code to individual FMOD event paths. The Setup window also detects FMOD for Unity and can migrate an Assets-based integration to an Embedded UPM package. Main features AudioSource-style event playback through FMODAudioSource. Searchable AMB, BGM, and SFX Global Key Lists. Per-GameObject Local Key Lists. Event or Key-based commands and Unity lifecycle triggers. Initial FMOD parameter overrides. FMOD installation detection and guarded Embedded UPM migration. Support for Fast Enter Play Mode. Start with Requirements, Installation, and Getting started. Note This documentation starts with FMOD Plus 1.7.0. Earlier releases remain available in the Changelog, but do not have separate manual versions.

manual/installation.html.title: Installation | FMOD Plus
manual/installation.html.summary: Installation Install FMOD for Unity under Assets first, add FMOD Plus through Git UPM, and then use the FMOD Plus Setup window to move FMOD to an Embedded UPM package. 1. Install FMOD for Unity under Assets Install FMOD for Unity using the standard FMOD Integration workflow. At this stage, keep the integration in its traditional Assets location: Assets/Plugins/FMOD Open the Unity project and wait for FMOD for Unity to finish importing. FMOD Plus does not include FMOD for Unity, FMOD Studio, banks, or an FMOD license. Important Complete this Assets-based FMOD installation before running the FMOD Plus migration. The Setup window searches the Assets installation and prepares it for the move to Packages. 2. Install FMOD Plus with Git UPM In Unity, open Window > Package Manager. Click + and choose Install package from git URL.... Enter the following URL and click Install: https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.fmodplus.git 3. Move FMOD to Packages After FMOD Plus has been installed successfully, open the following menu: FMOD > FMOD Plus > Setup The Setup window detects the FMOD Integration under Assets/Plugins/FMOD and displays the migration status, source version, target UPM version, destination, and GUID checks. Click Move FMOD to Packages. Review the confirmation dialog and continue with the migration. When the migration succeeds, the FMOD package is moved to: Packages/com.firelight.fmod-for-unity Project-specific FMOD Settings and Cache remain under Assets/Plugins/FMOD. Unity then recompiles the FMOD Plus Runtime and Editor assemblies against the detected FMOD package. Verify the installation After Unity finishes importing and compiling, verify that: Package Manager shows FMOD Plus and com.firelight.fmod-for-unity. FMOD > FMOD Plus > Setup reports the Embedded FMOD package as active. FMOD Plus components such as FMOD Audio Source are available. The Console has no FMOD or FMOD Plus compilation errors.

manual/key-lists.html.title: Global and Local Key Lists | FMOD Plus
manual/key-lists.html.summary: Global and Local Key Lists A Key List associates a string Key with an FMOD Event and its initial Local Parameter values. Instead of repeating Event paths across components, you can reuse names such as Stage1, Battle, or Footstep. Which Key List should you use? Type Storage Best suited for Global Key List Project Resources assets AMB, BGM, and SFX Events shared across Scenes LocalKeyList A Scene or Prefab GameObject Events used only by one Scene, Prefab, or feature AMB, BGM, and SFX are categories for organizing Keys and selecting which list to query. Registering a Key under BGM does not automatically route its Event to a BGM Bus. Configure the actual Bus routing in FMOD Studio. Create Global Key Lists Select FMOD > FMOD Plus > Global Key List from the Unity menu. When the window opens for the first time, it creates any missing assets at the following location: Assets/FMOD Plus Data/Resources/ ├── AMB-KeyList.asset ├── BGM-KeyList.asset └── SFX-KeyList.asset Select a category Use the AMB, BGM, and SFX buttons at the top of the window to select the list to edit. AMB: Organizes ambient sounds. BGM: Organizes background music. SFX: Organizes sound effects. The categories separate data only, so you can adapt their usage to your project's naming rules. Add and edit a Key Select the category to edit. Select Add Key to create an entry. Set its Key name in the detail panel. Select the linked Event in FMOD Event. Add initial values under Initial Parameters when needed. A new entry receives an available temporary name such as New Key or New Key (1). Rename it to describe its actual purpose. The list displays each Key and Event path. Select an entry to edit its actual data in the detail panel. Changing the Event clears the existing Initial Parameters so values from the previous Event cannot be mixed with the new one. Search The search field looks for Key names across AMB, BGM, and SFX. It performs a substring search. Search is case-insensitive. Each result displays its original category. Drag reordering is disabled during a search to protect the source indices. Selecting a category button clears the search and returns to that category. Important Search is case-insensitive, but runtime Key lookup is case-sensitive. Stage1 and stage1 are different Keys. Reorder and remove entries When no search is active, drag entries to change their order within the current category. Remove Key displays a confirmation dialog before deleting the selected entry. Adding, deleting, reordering, and editing Events or Parameters support Unity Undo/Redo. Modified Global assets are saved automatically. Edit Initial Parameters After selecting an Event, add its Local Parameters from Add Parameter. Select All to add every Parameter that is not already present. The editor displays an appropriate input for each FMOD Parameter type. FMOD Parameter type Editor control Continuous A floating-point Slider using the minimum and maximum range Discrete An integer Slider Labeled A Dropdown containing the FMOD labels These values are the initial values used when the Event is played through the Key. Removing a Parameter from the entry makes the Event use its FMOD default instead. If an Event cannot be found in the loaded banks, or a stored Parameter was removed from the Event, the editor displays Parameter Not Found. It does not discard the serialized data automatically. Select a new Event or remove obsolete entries manually. Create a Local Key List Create a LocalKeyList in either of the following ways: Select GameObject > Audio > FMOD > Key List. On an existing GameObject, select FMOD Studio > FMOD Plus > FMOD Local Key List from Add Component. The Local Key List Inspector uses the same basic workflow as the Global window. Select Add Key to add an entry. Set its Key name and FMOD Event. Add any required Initial Parameters. Search or drag entries to organize the list. Search is limited to the current LocalKeyList, and reordering is disabled while searching. Editing a Scene Object marks the Scene as changed. Editing a Prefab is recorded as a Prefab Override. Undo/Redo is also supported. Local Key List lookup API LocalKeyList can resolve an Event, its Parameters, or both together. using FMODPlus; using FMODUnity; using UnityEngine; public class LocalMusicLookup : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] private LocalKeyList keyList; [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource; public void Play(string key) { if (!keyList.TryGetEventAndParameters( key, out EventReference eventReference, out ParamRef[] parameters)) { Debug.LogWarning($"FMOD Key '{key}' was not found."); return; } audioSource.clip = eventReference; audioSource.ApplyParameter(parameters); audioSource.Play(); } } API Result Count Number of serialized Key entries TryGetEvent() Event Reference TryGetParameters() Initial ParamRef[] TryGetEventAndParameters() Event and Parameters together On failure, the methods return false, the Event is its default value, and Parameters are an empty array. Global Key List lookup API Global lists use one Singleton per category. using FMODPlus; using FMODUnity; using UnityEngine; public class GlobalMusicLookup : MonoBehaviour { public bool TryGetMusic( string key, out EventReference eventReference, out ParamRef[] parameters) { eventReference = default; parameters = System.Array.Empty<ParamRef>(); return BGMKeyList.Instance.TryGetValue(key, out eventReference) && BGMKeyList.Instance.TryGetParamRef(key, out parameters); } } AMBKeyList, BGMKeyList, and SFXKeyList provide the same lookup API. TryGetValue() returns the Event. TryGetParamRef() returns its initial Parameters. TryFindClip(), TryFindParamRefs(), and TryFindClipAndParams() perform equivalent lookups and log an error when they fail. Use the TryGet* methods when the caller should handle failure. Use the TryFind* methods when a missing Key must also be logged as an error. Global TryGetParamRef() can return null on failure, so check its Boolean result before using the array. Use KeyReference KeyReference packages a Global or Local list selection and its Key into one serializable value. using FMODPlus; using FMODUnity; using UnityEngine; public class KeyReferencePlayer : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] private KeyReference eventKey = new(); [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource; public void Play() { if (!eventKey.TryGetEventAndParameters( out EventReference eventReference, out ParamRef[] parameters)) { Debug.LogWarning($"FMOD Key '{eventKey.Key}' was not found."); return; } audioSource.clip = eventReference; audioSource.ApplyParameter(parameters); audioSource.Play(); } } TryGetEvent() resolves only the Event. TryGetEventAndParameters() also returns its initial values. Parameters are an empty array on failure, but always check the Boolean result before using them.

manual/requirements.html.title: Requirements | FMOD Plus
manual/requirements.html.summary: Requirements FMOD Plus is an extension for FMOD for Unity. It does not include FMOD Studio, FMOD for Unity, banks, or an FMOD license. Dependency Supported version Notes Unity 6000.3 or newer The current verified environment is Unity 6000.5.5f1. FMOD for Unity 2.02.0 or newer and earlier than 3.0.0 The package version define accepts UPM SemVer [2.2.0,3.0.0). The current verified environment uses FMOD 2.03.14. FMOD Plus detects the package named com.firelight.fmod-for-unity. When a supported version is present, it defines FMOD_PRESENT and enables the Runtime and Editor assemblies. Without a supported FMOD package, only the independent Setup bootstrap remains available. Licensing Install FMOD for Unity separately and follow FMOD's licensing and distribution terms. FMOD Plus itself is distributed under the license shown in the License section.

manual/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | FMOD Plus
manual/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting FMOD Plus components are missing Open FMOD > FMOD Plus > Setup. Confirm that com.firelight.fmod-for-unity is installed and its converted package version is in [2.2.0,3.0.0). Resolve the first Console error and allow Unity to recompile. The Setup window can remain available even when Runtime and Editor components are disabled because its bootstrap assembly does not reference FMOD. FMOD is installed under Assets Use Move FMOD to Packages in Setup. Review the preflight result before confirming. Do not manually regenerate FMOD.meta; its GUID must move with the integration. Banks or native plugins are missing Configure generated bank paths through the official FMOD settings. If platform native binaries are missing, use FMOD's Reorganize Plugin Files command when appropriate for that FMOD version. A Key does not resolve Verify the selected Global category or Local Key List, check that the key is not empty, and confirm the entry still has a valid Event Reference. Reopen the editor after Undo/Redo or asset changes if the displayed selection is stale.
